title: Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis (UTI in Women)
guideline: IDSA International Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Treatment of Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis

clinical_targets.goal: Disappearance of dysuria, urgency, and frequency within 48–72 hours
Avoid fluoroquinolones for simple cystitis to preserve collateral damage

steps.title: First-Line Targeted Antimicrobials
steps.rationale: High urinary concentration with minimal collateral disruption of intestinal flora.

drug_classes.role: First-line preferred agent with very low E. coli resistance rates.
drug_classes.dosing: Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals 100 mg twice daily with meals for 5 days.
drug_classes.pearls: Ineffective if eGFR < 30 mL/min (insufficient urinary concentration and risk of peripheral neuropathy). Ineffective for pyelonephritis.

drug_classes.dosing: Fosfomycin trometamol 3 g single-dose oral sachet mixed in water.
drug_classes.pearls: High urinary concentration sustained over 48 hours. Lower clinical cure rate than 5-day nitrofurantoin.

steps.title: Second-Line Oral Beta-Lactams
steps.rationale: Use when first-line agents are unavailable or contraindicated; slightly lower efficacy and higher GI side effects.

drug_classes.pearls: Avoid Ampicillin or Amoxicillin monotherapy due to very high worldwide E. coli resistance.

special_populations.renal_impairment: Do not use Nitrofurantoin if eGFR < 30 mL/min.
special_populations.pregnancy_lactation: Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy MUST be treated. Safe choices: Nitrofurantoin (avoid near term weeks 38–42 due to neonatal hemolysis), Amoxicillin/Clavulanate, or Cephalexin.

monitoring: Routine post-treatment urinalysis or urine culture is not indicated in asymptomatic patients.
